- **Onboarding & first 30 days**: no documented flow from sign-up through goal-setting, induction, first class, check-in cadence. Critical for retention.

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now** — Talk to your 5 best coaches and your 10 most loyal members separately. List every service/offering they mention (classes, PT, nutrition plans, challenges, etc.). You'll find gaps between what you think you offer and what's actually being sold. This is your honest baseline.

• **Build the member menu first, price backwards** — Start with what members care about (not coach logistics). Structure it like: *Membership tier* → *what classes/week* → *PT add-ons available* → *community perks*. Then price each tier so coaches can upsell PT profitably. Test pricing by showing 3 options to 10 members—pick the one people stop negotiating on.

• **Create a one-page coach "playbook" version** — Coaches need to know: which services they deliver, their commission/rate, what they can offer members without asking you, upsell triggers (e.g., "member hits 8 classes → offer PT trial"). Make it visual, not a document. Laminate it.

• **Lock it in Notion or a shared doc, not buried in emails** — Single source of truth. Include: service name, price, what's included, who delivers it, how long it takes. Update it monthly based on what actually sells. Share the member-facing version on your website/Instagram immediately—stop the "what do you offer?" DMs.

• **Use it as a sales tool THIS WEEK** — Every new member inquiry gets sent the menu before they visit. Coaches use it during inductions. Track which services get asked about most—those are your growth levers.
